title: Stale service discovery during Private control-plane rolling upgrade causes fallback to hosted endpoints for EU tenant
creator: Aisha Raman
description:
Summary: During a rolling upgrade of the Private control plane for customer EU-322, a subset of private service discovery entries (SRV records) were not refreshed. Smart-routing's fallback evaluator treated those private endpoints as unhealthy and routed requests to hosted API endpoints in us-west, resulting in increased latency, failed tenant-affinity guarantees, and an urgent customer escalation. The issue affected a steady fraction (~12%) of production requests for the customer's traffic window between 2026-03-01T03:10Z and 2026-03-01T06:45Z.

Impact: Tenant EU-322 observed: elevated p95 latency (2.8s -> 9.6s), 6m request routing to hosted models instead of tenant-dedicated pool, and temporary data residency concerns raised by their security team. No data exfiltration detected; requests were served by Redwood hosted models with equivalent model versions but different tenancy/egress controls.

Root cause: A race in the control-plane rolling restart path caused a subset of service discovery cache entries to persist across restart with stale health metadata. When the smart routing policy evaluated fallbacks, it merged discovery data and preferred the hosted pool due to a bug in the health-merge comparator (missing timestamp freshness). The merge incorrectly favored lower-latency historical health signals over freshly-reported but briefly-missing private endpoints.

Fix / Resolution summary: 1) Emergency hotfix deployed (runtime config toggle) to prefer tenant-scoped private endpoints over hosted pools while any private pool reported partial health; 2) code fix to the health-merge comparator to include last-updated timestamp and to avoid favoring stale records; 3) service discovery cache now performs an atomic replace on rolling restarts and flushes entries that are older than health_ttl; 4) added an observability check and alert (routing-stale-discovery) that fires when merged discovery sets contain >5% entries older than TTL; 5) customer communication and credits issued.

Follow-ups (in this ticket): implement pre-stop hooks to flush ephemeral discovery state on shutdown; add an e2e canary test that performs rolling upgrades in a dev-private cluster and validates no cross-tenant fallback occurs; schedule a security review for the hosted-routing fallbacks matrix.

References / Artifacts:
- Customer escalation (internal ticket): SUP-1127
- GitHub PR (hotfix): https://github.com/redwood-inference/control-plane/pull/3782
- GitHub PR (comparator fix + tests): https://github.com/redwood-inference/routing/pull/4120
- Postmortem draft (Confluence): https://confluence.redwood.ai/display/INC/ENG-98433+-+Private+SRV+stale+discovery+postmortem
- Monitoring dashboard: https://dashboard.redwood.ai/d/rt-routing/eu-private-routing
